result.note: Tests India's fertiliser import dependence and suppliers, the Hormuz chokepoint, and the 2026-27 fertiliser subsidy allocation.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the West Asia conflict disrupted India's fertiliser imports ahead of the kharif season. Consider the following statements:
items: India imports about 60% of its di-ammonium phosphate (DAP).
Saudi Arabia is India's biggest source of imported urea.
China's suspension of phosphate exports was in place until at least August 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Saudi Arabia is the top DAP supplier, while Oman is the biggest urea source. India also imports roughly half its urea, and the government held talks with Russia, Belarus and Morocco to fill the gap.
questions.source: Saudi Arabia is the top DAP supplier; Oman is the biggest urea source.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the West Asia conflict disrupted roughly half of India's DAP and urea imports. India's leading Gulf suppliers of both fertilisers ship through which waterway?
questions.explain: Both Saudi Arabia, the top DAP supplier, and Oman, the biggest urea source, ship through the Strait of Hormuz. Alternative cargoes from Russia and Belarus take weeks longer than Gulf routes.
questions.source: Both ship through the Strait of Hormuz.

questions.prompt: As of March 2026, before the West Asia conflict began, what had India's fertiliser subsidy bill for 2026-27 been set at?
questions.explain: The 2026-27 subsidy bill was set at INR 1.71 lakh crore (USD 20 billion) before the war. Urea prices have since surged about 50%, and rising import costs are expected to push the bill higher because the government shields farmers from global price spikes.
questions.source: But the subsidy bill for 2026-27 was already set at INR 1.71 lakh crore (USD 20 billion) before the war; rising import costs will push it higher.
